assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. dimensions.note: The opening section and the closing portrayal paragraph give an organizing principle: he asks what would make a decision commercially, professionally or publicly defensible, and decides which uncertainty 100 Pro will carry (R1-R6). Two predictions are kept separate. The narrower is a negotiated commercial exception, observed once and bounded to D-MAO: Mao and her Producer propose winning the winter H.I.F., he calls it a result others would recognize, acknowledges that a proven idol and a proven Producer together would have value to his company, grants a conditional exception to his staffing decision, and keeps that agreement after the win (R3). The broader prediction draws on both D-MAO and D-SENA: he revises a negative judgment when a concrete result disproves it and says so (he admits the pair has demonstrated its claim, R3; after Sena's audition distinctions he admits he was wrong, apologizes, retracts 'make-believe' and endorses her combined future, R12). R12 shows no prior commercial bargain and no staffing exception contingent on the result: he had already invited her Producer to continue after graduation, and he ended the audience without conceding, telling the Producer only that he looked forward to the proof. Further conditions are located once each: a request with limited direct benefit gets company consideration without a promise (R4); a professional's criticism counts as useful testimony even when it costs his side, and he gives no verdict where he holds no authority (R6); a concrete request to review terms that concern Mao's life gets time despite his dislike of waste (R3). The model predicts his mistakes and overreach: expecting Mao to accept his staffing decision (R2), judging the pair unable to beat Sena (R3), dismissing Sena's producing as make-believe (R12), professional address where the question is parental, and a judgment the hearer remembers as closing a path while he thinks he left a choice (R7-R8). Not A: one compact portrait; the commercial exception is a single Mao-bounded instance; persuasive paternal expectation remains a live counterreading of his path-paving principle (R7); his criterion and longer intention behind the remembered verdict on Sena's professional prospects are open (R8); the portrait gives no basis to infer he would often yield on a less concrete test (R3); there is no inner voice. The open family motives predict the same conduct toward Sena (pressure through the path he controls, revision on a demonstrated result), so they bound the model rather than leave the deciding factor unknown. Not C: the defensibility criterion discriminates his located responses to a recruit, a pair proposing a recognized test, a limited-benefit request and a critic (R1-R6); the revision of a disproved judgment is observed in two relationships (R3, R12); and the portrait states where each account stops.

Two located revisions with triggers. Within D-MAO, he moves from expecting Mao to accept his staffing and judging the pair unable to beat Sena to accepting them together after the winter result, while confining the defeat of Sena to that day (R2-R3). Within D-SENA, he moves from calling her producing make-believe to apologizing and endorsing her combined future after her audition distinctions (R12). His earlier failure with his first idol and his wife's warning are reported history (R7). Not B: these are revisions of judgment, not an ordered progression of his own condition; routes are alternate continuities, and later family history, including the proposed family meal, is open (R7). Not D: each change is located with its trigger and its before and after.

'Position, speech and reconstruction' gives a short written rule set: 私 in the cited professional and family-counsel exchanges; working peers addressed by role and prospective recruits by name with 君 or くん; firm declaratives alternating with compact questions about terms; his daughter addressed as 十王星南君 in the household interview, professional address where the question is parental (R8, R11). Located moves add a dry, demoting opening (the question 'sounds like a freshman's') that leads into a seriously offered personal reply (R5), the momentary pick-up of 'expulsion' before stating his purpose (R1), and an explicit dislike of wasted time (R3). Performed voice is limited to one scene-specific baritone observation on SRC-0026 (R11); no singing, characteristic music cue or continuous motion is identified. Not B: few quoted lines and no line inventory; the rules individuate an executive register mainly through address and question form, and the closing note names his warm or dry register toward family as untested by audible evidence. Not D: the address rules are located per listener and constrain illustrative written Japanese.

The portrait states that the admitted sources give limited ordinary conduct, age, health, tastes, leisure and later family history. Its narrow everyday anchors are infrequent family meetings, occasional attendance and the proposed family meal (R7), and one occasion of wearing Sena's `Campus mode!!` merchandise at a surprise audience, which it says establishes no ordinary hobby (R9). Not D: no distributed ordinary conduct outside work and two family occasions.

Differentiated conduct toward a recruit (title and name, existing skills as market value, the unsettled 'expulsion' pick-up, terms and time to consult her Producer and parents, R1); the recruit and her student Producer as a pair (removal on student status and different methods, then a conditional exception and a kept promise, R2-R3); a different student Producer, whom he judges capable and invites to continue with Sena after graduation (R12); another student Producer's project (company consideration, the risk named, no promise, R4); a student at a venue (a dry opening, then a personal answer, R5); a professional critic (useful testimony, no verdict, R6); his daughter (brusque judgment in professional address, dismissal, ending the audience, then apology and pride; attendance and the merchandise request, R8-R9, R12); and his wife by report (a warning he accepts from someone with family and professional standing, R7). The portrait states how his response changes with the relationship and with what is offered. Not A: most ties rest on one or two scenes; the wife and Kunio ties are reported or inferred (R7, R10), and staged private family conduct is thin. Not C: the conditioning is explicit and located across more than six relationship types.

No inner voice of his appears. Interior evidence is self-report: the account of childhood choices, his wife's warning and his failure with his first idol, given within a communication the portrait asks readers to separate into the Producer's report, embedded speech, attributed advice and Sena's response (R7); the personal view that the top idols he has seen loved idols and that a list of traits cannot define talent (R5); and his stated pleasure that Sena exceeded his forecast (R12). Observers' impressions (the Producer's inner speech, R4; Sena's account, R8) do not establish his thought. Not C: no direct interior access, and his wife's reasoning beyond his account is open (R7). Not E: the self-account connects his past failure to his present parenting, which is more than an isolated statement.

Located modes with triggers. Under a challenge from Mao and her Producer that turns his own objection to unsupported claims back on him and proposes a recognized result with value to 100 Pro, he names the condition and grants a conditional exception (R3, D-MAO only). When his daughter disputes his jurisdiction and offers to prove herself, he ends the audience without conceding and without striking any bargain, tells her Producer he looks forward to the proof, and retracts his judgment once it is delivered (R12). A concrete request to review terms that concern the recruit's life gets time despite his dislike of waste (R3). His rank can register as a threat without the scene settling his intent (R1). Not B: both full disputes involve a party he holds power over who offers to prove a claim, and only the Mao dispute becomes a negotiated exception; conflict with peers or rivals (Kuroi, Kunio over N.I.A.) is reported or inferred, not staged (R10), and no conflict without a proof route is shown. Not D: each mode carries its trigger and resolution.

Located positions with reasons: he keeps the condition he accepted with Mao and her Producer after the winter result (R3); he grants review because the terms concern Mao's life (R3); he accepts his wife's warning against loading his life onto a child's (R7); he apologizes for and retracts a disproved judgment of his daughter (R12); he counts a criticism as useful testimony and declines a formal verdict outside his authority (R6). Not B: his weighing is mostly commercial and shown from outside; his account of acting for Mao's wishes is partial, and he evaluates exposure by the agency's interests (R2); persuasive paternal expectation remains a live counterreading (R7). Not D: the positions are located with reasons across several routes.

Only two instances, both dry and one ambiguous: the momentary pick-up of 'expulsion', where the dialogue does not settle whether he intended a joke or a reminder of rank (R1), and the 'freshman's question' opening before a serious reply (R5). The merchandise request is presented as a family act, not as play (R9). Not D: no account of range or function beyond these two.

One compact, independently reviewed portrait (18,388 bytes) routes its claims to locators R1-R12 with script line ranges and names its absences (ordinary conduct, age, health, tastes, leisure, later family history, solo singing, music cues and motion). The audiovisual correction it links and the project's underlying readings are not curated on this subject. Not B: a single derived item without ledgers on the row. Not D: its routes cover the declared boundary.

Affirmative bounds and in-source corrections: the expulsion scene does not demonstrate institutional authority to expel (R1); the original offer did not make the Producer Mao's immediate producer (R2); his judgment that the pair could not beat Sena and his forecast for Sena were both overturned in the source, and he says so (R3, R12); he made no immediate promise to Rinami's Producer, and no agreement by Rinami is recorded (R4); no rule change and no control of Kunio's school follow from the Misuzu live (R6, R10); the Producer's imagined dismissal in Dear 029 is a counterfactual, not a firing (R12); one merchandise occasion establishes no hobby (R9); the grant of review time gives no basis to infer that he often yields (R3). Not A: the bounds are portrait statements without ledger-level forecast tests. Not C: several are corrected judgments of his own, located against specific overreadings (that he never changes his mind, controls the school or fired the Producer).

Each route keeps its own order and outcome (D-MAO from R1 through R2 to the winter result in R3; D-SENA from the remembered verdict through Dear 028 to Dear 033; D-RINAMI's Dear 030 and the later Dear 037 report), the separate communications and Event 028 stand alone, and his past is placed as reported history (R7). Not B: no calendar places his scenes on one timeline, and routes are alternate outcomes. Not D: route sequences and outcomes are located and kept apart.

conditions: Output is illustrative written Japanese, never quotation; no timbre, singing or performed delivery is claimed beyond the one scene-specific baritone observation (R11).

Register: 私; working peers by role; prospective recruits by name with 君 or くん; his daughter as 十王星南君 where the question is parental; firm declaratives alternating with compact questions about terms (R8, R11).
Moves: separating praise of ability from the timing or terms of an offer, asking what result would justify a risk, and a dry or demoting opening that can lead into a serious reply (R1-R5).

Interlocutors are the sampled ones: a recruit, a student Producer, a student at a venue, a professional critic and his daughter. A comparable agency executive or another school's student is a separate, lower-confidence condition limited to the register rules.
No domestic dialogue with his wife; his warm or dry register toward family is not established by audible evidence.
scenario_readiness.note: Address forms and question habits constrain illustrative written Japanese for him as 100 Pro's director with the sampled interlocutors closely enough for bounded use. Performed delivery and private family speech are not constrained.

conditions: A promising student he wants to sign: predict appraisal of existing skills as market value, an approach before other agencies, terms that distinguish early withdrawal from a provisional affiliation, staffing on agency criteria, and time to consult (R1-R2).

Mao and her Producer in D-MAO only, returning his objection to unsupported claims and proposing a concrete, publicly recognizable result with value to 100 Pro: predict a conditional exception to his staffing decision, scepticism about their present chances, and fidelity to the agreement if they deliver, with the win framed as the start of more work (R3). This negotiated bargain is observed once and is not predicted for any other challenger or for his daughter.

A concrete, demonstrated result that disproves a negative judgment he has voiced, with Mao and her Producer or with his daughter: predict that he admits the error and revises the judgment (R3, R12). With his daughter no prior bargain, authorization or staffing exception is predicted (R12).
A request with limited direct benefit to 100 Pro: predict company consideration, the risk named, a possible later gain weighed, and no immediate promise (R4).
A professional's criticism of a contest he helped arrange: predict that it counts as useful testimony and that he proposes correcting rules, with no formal verdict where he holds no authority (R6).

His daughter's career choices: predict a brusque judgment in professional address, possible dismissal of what she claims, ending the exchange without conceding or bargaining while saying he looks forward to her proof, then apology and endorsement if she delivers (R8, R12).

Include his mistakes: assuming acceptance of his staffing decision, underrating a pair before the result, a judgment heard as closing a path, and rank pressure whose intent he leaves unsettled (R1-R3, R7-R8, R12).

Exclude any prediction that he yields on a less concrete test, that a challenger other than Mao and her Producer wins a negotiated commercial exception, his conduct in conflict with peers or rivals, decisions at Hatsuboshi, and his role in designing N.I.A. (R3, R10, R12).

known_limits.statement: All claims rest on one 18,388-byte derived portrait; most relationships rest on one or two scenes, and no held-out test of its portrayal guidance is reported.

His account of paving a path and leaving the later decision to Sena leaves persuasive paternal expectation as a live counterreading, and his criterion and longer intention behind the remembered verdict on her professional prospects are open (R7-R8).

The negotiated exception and the grant of review time (R3) and the retraction toward Sena (R12) all follow concrete tests; the portrait says this gives no basis to infer that he would often yield on a less concrete test or that his preferred risks match a recruit's (R3).

The negotiated commercial exception is observed once, in D-MAO, where he recognizes winter H.I.F. as a public test with value to 100 Pro and honors the staffing agreement after Mao wins (R3). Sena's route shows no prior bargain and no staffing exception contingent on the result: he had already invited her Producer to continue after graduation, and after her audition distinctions he revises his judgment of her (R12). R12 supports the broader revision of a disproved judgment, not a second instance of the bargain.
Whether the 'expulsion' pick-up was a joke or a deliberate reminder of rank is unsettled, and the scene demonstrates no institutional authority to expel (R1).

His wife's warning and acting career are known from his account within a communication that mixes the Producer's report and embedded speech; their later meal and her reasoning beyond his account are open (R7).

That Kunio's son who devised N.I.A. with Kuroi is Ryuusei is highly plausible but not stated; the portrait does not establish that he runs Hatsuboshi by proxy or that school and agency apply one standard (R10).
The one baritone observation on SRC-0026 is scene-specific; no solo singing, characteristic music cue, representative movement, facial tension or person-wide affect profile is established (R11).
Age, health, tastes, leisure, home routine, staged marriage and later family history are outside the evidence.
The audiovisual correction linked from R11, the project's source-facing readings and ledgers and its qualification record are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them.
